title: E91 and Entanglement-Based QKD
description: Ekert's protocol, Bell's theorem and the CHSH inequality for security

questions.question: The E91 protocol was introduced in 1991 by
options: Artur Ekert
Charles Bennett
Peter Shor
Charles Bennett and Artur Ekert
questions.correctAnswer: Artur Ekert

questions.question: In E91, the entangled photon pairs are produced by
options: a source that sends one photon of each pair to Alice and the other to Bob
Alice, who prepares them and sends them to Bob over a quantum link
Bob, who measures one member and forwards the other to Alice
a satellite that stores the pairs until both parties are ready
questions.correctAnswer: a source that sends one photon of each pair to Alice and the other to Bob

questions.question: The entangled pairs used in E91 are the physical realisation of
options: Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pairs, whose members have correlated but individually undefined properties
Bohm-Aaronson pairs, designed to violate Bell inequalities
Schrödinger cat states, superpositions of macroscopic objects
Cooper pairs, which bind electrons in a superconductor
questions.correctAnswer: Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pairs, whose members have correlated but individually undefined properties

questions.question: Bell's theorem shows that
options: no theory of local hidden variables can reproduce all the predictions of quantum mechanics
quantum mechanics can never be verified experimentally to arbitrary precision
local hidden variable theories agree with quantum mechanics only for entangled states
every experiment that tests Bell's inequality must support local realism
questions.correctAnswer: no theory of local hidden variables can reproduce all the predictions of quantum mechanics

questions.question: The CHSH inequality is a testable statement of the form
options: $|S| \le 2$ for any local hidden variable theory
$|S| \le 1$ for any local hidden variable theory
$|S| \le 4$ for any local hidden variable theory
$|S| \ge 2$ for any local hidden variable theory
questions.correctAnswer: $|S| \le 2$ for any local hidden variable theory

questions.question: For maximally entangled states, the CHSH parameter can reach
options: $2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83$, which exceeds the classical bound of $2$
$2$, exactly equal to the classical bound
$4$, the largest value the inequality allows
$\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41$, below the classical bound
questions.correctAnswer: $2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83$, which exceeds the classical bound of $2$

questions.question: In E91, Alice and Bob each measure using
options: a random choice from three bases, two of which supply the key and one of which is used for the Bell test
a random choice from two bases, both of which supply the key
a single basis fixed by the protocol, so the key is deterministic
a random choice from four bases, all of which supply the key
questions.correctAnswer: a random choice from three bases, two of which supply the key and one of which is used for the Bell test

questions.question: In E91, an eavesdropper is detected because she
options: must interact with the entangled photons, which breaks the correlations tested by Bell's inequality
must switch off the entangled source, which is immediately noticed
must add photons to the channel, which raises the detection rate
must measure in one of the three bases, which changes the sifted key length
questions.correctAnswer: must interact with the entangled photons, which breaks the correlations tested by Bell's inequality

questions.question: Why does a violation of the CHSH inequality signal eavesdropping in E91?
options: with ideal devices the observed correlations are the entangled ones, so a departure from them can only come from outside interference
a CHSH violation always indicates that the detectors are misaligned
Eve's presence forces $S$ below the classical bound of $2$
Bell's inequality is violated by any quantum signal that is merely transmitted
questions.correctAnswer: with ideal devices the observed correlations are the entangled ones, so a departure from them can only come from outside interference

questions.question: Which measurements in E91 provide the shared key?
options: those in the two bases not reserved for the Bell test, keeping the settings that satisfy the required correlation condition
only those in the third basis, which is used for the Bell test
all measurements, since every setting yields an identical bit
only those in which Alice and Bob chose the same basis
questions.correctAnswer: those in the two bases not reserved for the Bell test, keeping the settings that satisfy the required correlation condition

questions.question: The essential difference between E91 and BB84 is that
options: E91 uses entangled pairs shared by the two parties, while BB84 uses a single prepare-and-measure channel
E91 uses four bases, while BB84 uses two
E91 needs no authenticated classical channel, while BB84 does
E91 encodes two bits per photon, while BB84 encodes one
questions.correctAnswer: E91 uses entangled pairs shared by the two parties, while BB84 uses a single prepare-and-measure channel

questions.question: E91 is a candidate for device-independent QKD because
options: its security can be established from observed correlations alone, without trusting the internal operation of the devices
it needs no entangled source and can therefore run in any laboratory
it operates entirely over classical channels
it guarantees that Eve cannot intercept the photons
questions.correctAnswer: its security can be established from observed correlations alone, without trusting the internal operation of the devices

questions.question: The main experimental obstacle to device-independent QKD is
options: the very high detection efficiency and low loss needed to close the detection loophole
the fact that Bell's inequality cannot be tested in a laboratory
the absence of any established theory of quantum entanglement
the impossibility of building entangled photon sources at all
questions.correctAnswer: the very high detection efficiency and low loss needed to close the detection loophole

questions.question: A Bell test used to certify security must be designed to
options: close the locality and detection loopholes, otherwise the violation can be explained classically
repeat each measurement only once, to avoid perturbing the state
avoid repeating the experiment, since repetition reduces the violation
measure all photons in a single basis, to maximise the count rate
questions.correctAnswer: close the locality and detection loopholes, otherwise the violation can be explained classically

questions.question: In E91, Alice and Bob can check that their photons really were entangled by
options: testing whether the observed correlations violate a Bell inequality for more than one pair of settings
counting the photons that arrive at each detector
comparing the arrival times of the two photons
measuring the polarisation of the entangled source directly
questions.correctAnswer: testing whether the observed correlations violate a Bell inequality for more than one pair of settings

questions.question: For an entangled pair, each photon's individual polarisation is
options: completely random, while the pair's joint results are strongly correlated
fixed at the moment of creation and merely unknown to the observers
random and completely uncorrelated with that of its partner
determined only after both detectors have been read out
questions.correctAnswer: completely random, while the pair's joint results are strongly correlated

questions.question: Bell's theorem relies on the locality assumption that
options: a measurement on one wing cannot instantaneously influence the outcome at the distant wing
all particles communicate only through a classical field
measurements are local, but the outcomes are fixed by a shared random table
quantum influences propagate only at the speed of light
questions.correctAnswer: a measurement on one wing cannot instantaneously influence the outcome at the distant wing

questions.question: A further assumption in Bell tests is that the measurement settings are chosen
options: randomly and independently of the source, which closes the freedom-of-choice loophole
so that both parties always choose the same settings
as late as possible, after the photons have already been detected
according to a fixed schedule known to the source in advance
questions.correctAnswer: randomly and independently of the source, which closes the freedom-of-choice loophole

questions.question: In an E91 run, the parties abort when the measured
options: CHSH parameter falls below the value required to certify a secure key
photon count falls below the bandwidth of the classical channel
polarisation drift exceeds the birefringence limit of the fibre
key length exceeds the memory of the random number generator
questions.correctAnswer: CHSH parameter falls below the value required to certify a secure key

questions.question: A further application of entangled-pair experiments is
options: certified randomness, in which the observed Bell violation guarantees that the bits are unpredictable
local randomness generation, which needs no quantum hardware
deterministic computation of a random seed from a classical hash
secure storage of random numbers against quantum attacks
questions.correctAnswer: certified randomness, in which the observed Bell violation guarantees that the bits are unpredictable

questions.question: The DiVincenzo criteria list the conditions a physical device must satisfy to run a quantum cryptography protocol, including
options: the ability to initialise, manipulate and read out qubits, together with isolation from the environment
a classical public key and an equally long private key
the ability to perform fast integer factoring on demand
a guarantee of noiseless transmission over any distance
questions.correctAnswer: the ability to initialise, manipulate and read out qubits, together with isolation from the environment

questions.question: Compared with BB84, the security analysis of E91 is
options: expressed directly in terms of observed Bell violations and entropic quantities
expressed in terms of the size of the RSA modulus used for authentication
based on the difficulty of finding preimages of a hash function
based on directly counting the number of photons an eavesdropper removed
questions.correctAnswer: expressed directly in terms of observed Bell violations and entropic quantities
